card.name: Biguine
card.profile: Biguine is a rhythmic dance and music style of the French Antilles, originating in Saint-Pierre, Martinique in the 19th century and shared with Guadeloupe. It fuses West African bele drumming with 19th-century French ballroom dance steps; the orchestrated biguine is defined by the interplay of clarinet and trombone, while the drum biguine (bidgin bele) uses the bele drum and tibwa sticks with call-and-response nasal singing. Danced as a close couple dance with a roll of the hips. It reached Paris after the 1931 Colonial Exhibition via stars like Alexandre Stellio and Sam Castandet (Wikipedia; Smithsonian Folkways).
card.insight: Biguine is widely cited as one of the ancestors of the jazz developed by Creoles of New Orleans. Cole Porter composed 'Begin the Beguine' in 1935; it gained fame chiefly via Artie Shaw's 1938 swing arrangement, a best-selling record (Wikipedia).
